name: New York

dates.sub: That day you can register and vote early at the same time.
Online or by mail. In person at your county board by Nov 2.
Postmarked by Nov 3 and received by Nov 10.

groups.title: Federal
groups.sub: They make laws for the entire country.

groups.title: State
groups.sub: They run New York. Everyone in the state votes on these.

groups.title: State lawmakers
groups.sub: They write New York's laws. Your district decides who's on your ballot.

footerNote: If your address can't be matched, we fall back to ZIP code. ZIP codes can cross district lines, so double-check yours on your voter page.

notes.title: Why some names show up twice.
notes.text: In New York, a candidate can run on more than one party's line, like Democrat and Working Families, or Republican and Conservative. Pick them on any one of their lines and it counts the same.

notes.title: Live in New York City?
notes.text: Your ballot also has 5 yes-or-no questions about changing the City Charter, the city's rulebook.
